question: The inequality \(y-x\lt\sqrt{x^2}\) is satisfied if and only if
solution:
For every real \(x\), the principal square root satisfies \(\sqrt{x^2}=|x|\). Adding \(x\) to both sides turns the given inequality into
\[
y<x+|x|.
\]
We now use the sign of \(x\) to remove the absolute value.

If \(x\ge0\), then \(|x|=x\), so the condition is \(y<2x\). Because \(2x\ge0\), any \(y<0\) already satisfies \(y<2x\). Thus in this case, “\(y<0\) or \(y<2x\)” is exactly the required condition.

If \(x<0\), then \(|x|=-x\), so the condition is \(y<0\). Because \(2x<0\), any \(y<2x\) already satisfies \(y<0\). The same inclusive-or statement is therefore equivalent in this case too.

These cases cover every real \(x\), including \(x=0\), where the condition is \(y<0\). The answer is \(y<0\) or \(y<2x\), choice A.
